title: Vocal Jazz: line-check the wireless mics
about: First gameplay slice (PRODUCT_DESIGN.md sections 46 and 94): one signal chain (handheld -> receiver -> X32 input), one fault (a handheld powered on but muted), one objective that completes only on verified evidence, one hint ladder, one debrief. Everything marked tentative or unknown below is a placeholder to field-calibrate, not room truth.

clock.status: tentative: 4:50 doors / 5:00 rehearsal come from PRODUCT_DESIGN section 40; the per-action and per-move seconds are placeholders (section 89 says movement-time scaling is field-calibrate)

setup.status: scenario sizing chosen for a short slice, not a claim about how many mics Vocal Jazz uses
setup.note: X32 and receivers start powered on so that the transmitter mute is the only fault (one fault per section 94).

ptu6000-rx.label: Phenyx Pro PTU-6000 receivers
ptu6000-rx.unknown: how the channels are split across the physical receiver units, and whether a muted transmitter still shows RF on the receiver. Only audio present / absent is modelled.

devices_status: Handhelds 1-8 have black windscreens (PRODUCT_DESIGN section 26, current fact). Their exact colour-ring order is unknown and not modelled. Handhelds live in the FOH mic drawer (manifest row IMG_4127).

handheld_button.status: tentative: the reference says 'single button = power / tap-to-mute'; reading the power gesture as press-and-hold is an assumption

mute_survives_power_cycle.status: unknown: not documented for these handhelds. true means switching a muted mic off and on does NOT clear the mute. Confirm in the room.

muted_indication.value: state shown in words on inspect
muted_indication.status: unknown: what the real transmitter shows when muted (LED, display) is not documented, so the slice only reports it as state

connections_status: Path shape is current fact: handheld -> PTU-6000 -> XLR -> X32 local analog input (PRODUCT_DESIGN section 37). The one-to-one numbering (handheld N -> receiver channel N -> X32 input N) is tentative: section 24 says wireless mics normally occupy channels 1-16, section 47 marks the layout field-calibrate.

fault.label: A wireless handheld is powered on but muted
fault.target: one handheld in play, chosen by the seed

objective.label: Line-check the wireless mics
objective.goal: Every mic in play is verified: talking into it shows signal at its X32 input.
objective.source: PRODUCT_DESIGN sections 45 (speak into each mic), 55 (goals, not recipes; complete only after verification)

hints.text: No signal is reaching the receiver. Where could the problem be upstream?
The transmitter is muted. Unmute it and verify signal.
